notes.text: Nearly all of the roughly 50 million active US mortgages carry fixed rates, most of them far below prevailing market rates, so policy-rate rises pass through to new buyers but barely touch existing owners. FHFA researchers estimate that each percentage point by which market rates exceed a borrower's locked-in rate cuts the probability of selling by 18.1%, which reduced fixed-rate home sales by 57% in 2023Q4 and prevented 1.33 million sales between 2022Q2 and 2023Q4.

sources.title: The Lock-In Effect of Rising Mortgage Rates (Working Paper 24-03)

notes.text: Rate lock-in works as a supply shock: by keeping owners in place it shrinks the resale stock, and FHFA estimates this lifted house prices by 5.7%, more than offsetting the 3.3% drag from higher borrowing costs. The homeowner vacancy rate stood at 1.2% in the third quarter of 2026, little changed from a year earlier, which keeps for-sale inventory tight.

Quarterly Residential Vacancies and Homeownership, Third Quarter 2026

notes.text: The rental market has loosened: the national rental vacancy rate rose from 5.6% in the second quarter of 2022 to 7.6% in the third quarter of 2026, above its year-earlier level of 7.1%. Higher vacancy reduces landlords' pricing power and restrains rent growth.

sources.title: Quarterly Residential Vacancies and Homeownership, Third Quarter 2026

notes.text: Mortgage credit is anchored by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which can only acquire loans up to the conforming loan limit; for 2026 that limit is USD 832,750 for a one-unit home in most of the country and up to USD 1,249,125 in high-cost areas. The limit rises each year in line with FHFA's house price index (3.26% for 2026), so government-backed securitisation keeps pace with prices.

sources.title: FHFA Announces Conforming Loan Limit Values for 2026

notes.text: The FHFA House Price Index is a weighted repeat-sales index of single-family homes whose mortgages were purchased or securitised by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac, published monthly and quarterly from national down to census-tract level. Because it relies on conforming loans, it under-represents jumbo-loan and all-cash segments; FHFA's expanded-data version adds FHA and county recorder sales.
